scenarios.note: All four critical states have current direct sensors with independent physical, calibration, power, communication, clock and measurement-principle domains.
One required junction pressure sensor is physically failed; no alternate independent channel or qualified estimator exists.
Two nominally separate level channels share one calibration lineage; a calibration-domain fault invalidates both and must not earn redundancy credit.
Two different measurement principles still share a common UPS; a power-domain failure invalidates both.
Separate sensors routed through the same gateway are not independent against gateway loss.
A common clock-domain drift makes both time-dependent level observations invalid; they are indeterminate, not two agreeing measurements.
All sensor channels are available, but the structural certificate is bound to an earlier topology revision/digest and must not be reused.
The topology-only structural test passes, but the numerical estimator for tank_level_2 is badly conditioned and its interval evidence is insufficient.
The topology/state mapping omits a required junction pressure binding; a structural result cannot certify the full required state set.
A second pressure channel has independent physical, calibration, power, communication, clock and measurement-principle dependencies, so it survives the primary calibration-domain failure.
Tank level 2 has no direct sensor; a fully referenced synthetic estimator contract meets the fixture's scope, holdout, interval and OOD requirements. No physical qualification is claimed.
No topology-bound structural certificate has been verified; direct sensor values may exist but they cannot establish network-wide observability under this contract.

interpretation_rules: Structural observability is conditional on the exact network topology and required-state mapping; a certificate for another revision/digest is invalid.
A measurement channel is independently surviving only when its own condition, calibration, time status and every active failure-domain dependency permit it.
Two sensors sharing an active physical, calibration, power, communications, clock or measurement-principle failure domain do not count as independent redundancy.
A structural full result without a numerically qualified estimator is structural_observable_only for an unmeasured state, not a positive state estimate.

An estimator can be marked synthetic_qualified_contract only when the fixture contains model scope, calibration, held-out and OOD references; coverage, sample count, interval width and conditioning bounds meet the synthetic profile. This does not claim physical qualification.
A common clock fault invalidates time alignment; do not treat agreeing stale measurements as current direct observations.
All IDs, topologies, failure domains, measurements and thresholds are synthetic and non-normative.
The benchmark consumes candidate layouts from Symtropy #4006; it does not implement another sensor-layout optimizer.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic observability-qualification challenge only. No real WDN topology, sensor, estimator or hydraulic state is qualified.
